assertions.assertion: Exactly three Synthetic Tenants are accepted and P1 decisions are never production reusable.
DraftArtifact is complete, RFC 8785 canonicalized and SHA-256 frozen; differences, sources and risks are server-computed.
A changed recipient object or a changed frozen Workflow Catalog version changes the binding and invalidates the old decision.
Chat consent, Stage Approval, LangGraph Interrupt and ordinary button fields are not a decision.
Prepare, approve, withdraw and execute use operation-specific C06 decisions; C05 is resolved before and after C06, then C03 admits the Tenant.
Expiry, withdrawal, authority revocation, an unbound current leaf delegation and tampering fail closed; a valid renewed leaf is reauthorized.
Effect and Audit records use transactional Outboxes, named idempotency constraints, stable IDs, token-bound expired-lease reclaim, ACK-loss retry and fresh-PostgreSQL recoverable state.

C0 Synthetic commit is followed by independent readback; mismatch enters compensation or compensation-failed state, successful compensation is read back again, and compensation retry converges after ACK loss.
Network, enterprise credentials, arbitrary URLs and real external effects remain absent.

An owner-preserving restore into a PostgreSQL cluster with a different system identifier retains C15 object ownership, removes PUBLIC access, enforces FORCE RLS on all eight tables, preserves exact runtime/effect/audit/recovery function and table privileges, signed transaction scope, append-only history and paired transaction guards.

Audit publication is accepted only after a real C18 PostgreSQL CommandReceipt and AuditEvent are persisted and bound to the same Tenant and C15 Intent; retry after a lost C15 ACK reuses the same C18 Event.

Effect and Audit workers have no direct table UPDATE capability; security-definer functions require the exact live lease token, and PostgreSQL independently rejects fabricated terminal receipts or Audit authority bindings.
